# TODO

Project task tracking for aidevops framework.

Compatible with [todo-md](https://github.com/todo-md/todo-md), [todomd](https://github.com/todomd/todo.md), [taskell](https://github.com/smallhadroncollider/taskell), [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads), and TOON-enhanced parsing.

## Format

**Human-readable:**

```markdown
- [ ] tXXX Task description @owner #tag ~4h (ai:2h test:1h read:30m) logged:2025-01-15
  - [ ] tXXX.1 Subtask ~2h blocked-by:tYYY
    - [ ] tXXX.1.1 Sub-subtask ~1h
  - [ ] tXXX.2 Another subtask ~1h blocks:tZZZ
- [x] tYYY Completed task ~2h actual:1.5h logged:2025-01-10 completed:2025-01-15
- [-] tZZZ Declined task
```

**Recurring routines:**

```markdown
## Routines

- [x] r001 Weekly SEO rankings export repeat:weekly(mon@09:00) ~30m run:custom/scripts/seo-export.sh
- [x] r002 Daily health check repeat:daily(@06:00) ~2m run:custom/scripts/health-check.sh
- [ ] r003 Monthly content calendar review repeat:monthly(1@09:00) ~15m agent:Content
- [x] r004 Nightly repo triage repeat:cron(15 2 * * *) ~20m agent:Build+
- [x] r005 Daily worktree cleanup repeat:daily(@03:00) ~5m run:scripts/worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged
- [x] r006 Hourly stub-title issue scanner repeat:cron(15 * * * *) ~2m run:custom/scripts/r-stub-title-scan.sh
```

**Task ID format:**

- `t001` - Top-level task
- `t001.1` - Subtask of t001
- `t001.1.1` - Sub-subtask of t001.1
- IDs are stable and never reused

**Routine ID format:**

- `r001` - Top-level recurring routine definition
- `r002` - Another recurring routine definition
- `r`-prefix IDs distinguish routines from `t`-prefix tasks
- IDs are stable and never reused

**Dependency fields:**

- `blocked-by:t001,t002` - This task cannot start until t001 and t002 are done
- `blocks:t003,t004` - Completing this task unblocks t003 and t004
- `parent:t001` - This is a child of t001 (implicit from indentation)

**Time fields:**

- `~estimate` - Total time estimate with optional breakdown `(ai:Xh test:Xh read:Xm research:Xm)`
- `actual:` - Actual time spent (recorded at commit/release)
- `logged:` - When task was added
- `started:` - When branch was created (work began)
- `completed:` - When task was marked done

**Routine fields:**

- `[x]` - Routine enabled; pulse/schedulers may dispatch it
- `[ ]` - Routine disabled or paused; pulse skips it
- `repeat:` - Human-readable schedule: `daily(@HH:MM)`, `weekly(day@HH:MM)`, `monthly(N@HH:MM)`, or `cron(expr)`
- `run:` - Script path relative to `~/.aidevops/agents/` for pure-script routines that should run without LLM tokens
- `agent:` - Agent name for LLM-backed routines dispatched via `headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- Dispatch rule: `run:` wins over `agent:` when both are present
- Default dispatch: if neither field is set, use `run:custom/scripts/{routine-name}.sh` when that script exists, otherwise `agent:Build+`

**Assignment fields:**

- `assignee:identity` - Who claimed the task (set by `supervisor-helper.sh claim`, identity = `AIDEVOPS_IDENTITY` or `user@host`)
- `@owner` - Who is responsible for the task (separate from assignee — future feature)

**Machine data:** TOON blocks in HTML comments (invisible when rendered).

2.0,todo-md+toon+beads,2025-12-21T16:00:00Z
-->

## Routines

- [x] r-gh-audit-scan Scan gh-audit.log for anomalies repeat:daily(@09:00) run:scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan
- [x] r040 Knowledge review gate — classify inbox items by trust, auto-promote or review-file repeat:cron(*/15 * * * *) ~1m run:scripts/knowledge-review-helper.sh tick
- [x] r041 Knowledge enrichment — extract structured fields from freshly-promoted sources repeat:cron(*/30 * * * *) ~2m run:scripts/document-enrich-helper.sh tick
- [x] r042 Knowledge index build — incremental PageIndex tree across corpus repeat:cron(*/60 * * * *) ~2m run:scripts/knowledge-index-helper.sh build
- [x] r044 IMAP mailbox polling — fetch new emails to _knowledge/inbox/ repeat:cron(*/10 * * * *) ~1m run:scripts/email-poll-helper.sh tick
- [x] r043 Case deadline alarming — classify open-case deadlines, fire gh-issue + ntfy alarms by stage repeat:cron(*/15 * * * *) ~1m run:scripts/case-alarm-helper.sh tick
- [x] r045 Email filter tick: auto-attach matched email sources to cases repeat:cron(*/15 * * * *) run:scripts/email-filter-helper.sh tick
- [x] r046 Canonical-recovery sweep — re-attempt failed git pull/stash for repos with active advisory files (t3027) repeat:cron(*/10 * * * *) ~1m run:scripts/canonical-recovery-routine.sh tick
- [ ] r047 Knowledge collector freshness — execute due read-only sources and emit content-free health repeat:cron(*/10 * * * *) ~2m run:scripts/knowledge-collector-routine.sh run
- [ ] r-runtime-audit Runtime health audit — surface operational regressions invisible to the supervisor LLM (counter trends, process leaks, deploy mtime drift, log novelty, stuck pulse state) (t3072) repeat:cron(*/30 * * * *) ~2m run:scripts/runtime-health-audit-helper.sh --apply
- [x] r-pulse-check Daily pulse/worker utilisation check — aggregate repos.json auto-dispatch queue, active capacity, provider/API budget, and file deduplicated self-improvement issues for high-confidence productivity gaps repeat:daily(@06:20) ~5m run:scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh apply

- [x] t2559 fix(worktree-cleanup): harden against empty main_worktree_path — 2026-04-20 canonical trash incident — `worktree-helper.sh::cmd_clean` derives `main_worktree_path` from `git worktree list --porcelain` without validating non-empty; when the porcelain output is empty (git missing, transient failure, stdout bleed), the downstream "never touch main" guard `[[ $worktree_path != $main_wt_path ]]` collapses to `[[ $worktree_path != "" ]]` — always true for real paths — and canonical gets swept alongside orphans. Canonical `~/Git/aidevops` was trashed at 2026-04-20 23:50:01; co-incident: `pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh:334` ANSI-bleed arithmetic crash from colored stdout leaking into `$((sweep_count + removed))` where `$removed` captured the full banner plus the printf int. Four-layer defensive fix: **L1** empty-derivation guard in `cmd_clean` — refuse when porcelain is empty or `main_worktree_path` is non-absolute. **L2** `is_registered_canonical` allowlist check against `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` `.initialized_repos[].path` in BOTH `trash_path` (worktree-helper.sh) and `_trash_or_remove` (pulse-cleanup.sh) — fail-safe: on ambiguity (unresolvable path, missing jq, malformed json), treat as canonical. **L3** `assert_git_available` at every cleanup entry point — refuse if git is missing from PATH. **L4** primary ANSI-bleed fix: redirect `worktree-helper.sh clean` stdout to `$LOGFILE` (not `/dev/null` — preserve diagnostics) inside `_stale_worktree_sweep_single_repo`, preventing banner bleed into the captured `printf '%d'`; defense-in-depth: `$removed` sanitisation (`${val//[^0-9]/}; val=${val:-0}`) in `_stale_worktree_sweep` so any future regression produces arithmetic-safe garbage instead of pulse crash. NEW: `.agents/scripts/canonical-guard-helper.sh` (`is_registered_canonical`, `assert_git_available`, `assert_main_worktree_sane`), `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-trash-guard.sh` (16 assertions: allowlist positive/negative/empty/trailing-slash/env-extra, sanity asserts for both git-available and main-sane variants, ANSI-bleed arithmetic safety across 3 poisoning shapes, end-to-end `trash_path` refusal + non-canonical regression guard). EDIT: `worktree-helper.sh` (trash_path + cmd_clean), `pulse-cleanup.sh` (_trash_or_remove + _cleanup_merged_prs_for_all_repos), `pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh` (_stale_worktree_sweep_single_repo + _stale_worktree_sweep). @marcusquinn #bug #framework #security #interactive ~3h tier:standard ref:GH#20205 logged:2026-04-21 -> [todo/tasks/t2559-brief.md] pr:#20209 completed:2026-04-21

- [x] t2570 feat(scanner): detect empty-compare foot-gun bash pattern — post-t2559 follow-up. Scanner at `.agents/scripts/empty-compare-scanner.sh` detects `[[ "$x" != "$y" ]]` / `[[ "$x" == "$y" ]]` (and `[ ... ]` variants) where `$y` is populated from command substitution or parameter expansion and the RHS lacks a prior non-empty assertion in the same function scope. Canonical failure: 2026-04-20 issue #20068 (t2430, tagged `#parent`) created at 02:35:51Z; peer runner alex-solovyev dispatched a worker at 02:36:39Z (+48s); `parent-task` label not applied until maintainer intervention ~03:34Z. Worker released cleanly after intervention but the race is adversarial in multi-runner fleets (the exact environment t2422 hardens). Root cause: three-way timing gap — (1) `claim-task-id.sh` fallback path drops labels, (2) `gh_create_issue` has no TODO-tag awareness, (3) label sync is workflow-deferred. **Approach A (preferred):** synchronous TODO tag → label resolution at issue creation — extract `_derive_labels_from_tags()` from `issue-sync-helper.sh` to `issue-sync-lib.sh` as shared resolver; add `--todo-task-id tNNN` flag to `gh_create_issue` to scan TODO.md and apply derived labels atomically. **Approach B (safety net):** `DISPATCH_HYDRATION_WINDOW_S=30` in `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` skipping dispatch on issues <30s old. Recommended: A + B. Acceptance: issue with `#parent` TODO tag has `parent-task` label IMMEDIATELY at creation (before any TODO.md push); peer-runner pulse within 30s sees `PARENT_TASK_BLOCKED`; regression test `tests/test-parent-tag-sync.sh` covers all three scenarios. @marcusquinn #bug #framework #multi-runner #interactive ~3h tier:standard ref:GH#20081 logged:2026-04-20 pr:#20117 completed:2026-04-20

(2) `memory-pressure-monitor.sh:464-465` still uses `${var,,}` in production code with a comment explicitly justifying Bash 4+ — local linter flags it, CI doesn't (CI has a narrower check set than the local linter, which is its own bug). (3) 69 `local -n` nameref lines across `compare-models-helper.sh` (43), `email-delivery-test-helper.sh` (12), `document-creation-helper.sh` (11), under an accepted ratchet of 72 — scripts silently break mid-execution on Bash 3.2 instead of failing fast with a readable error. (4) `reference/bash-compat.md:14` only documents the double-letter forms, which is how the single-letter variants propagated into the scanner regex. Fix extends both scanners to match single-letter forms, converts `memory-pressure-monitor.sh` to the documented `tr` pattern, adds `BASH_VERSINFO` guards to the three nameref scripts, expands the doc to list all four forms explicitly, and files t2024/t2025/t2026 as burn-down follow-ups. #bug #bash-compat #interactive ~2.5h tier:standard ref:GH#18489 logged:2026-04-13 -> [todo/tasks/t2023-brief.md] pr:#18490 completed:2026-04-13

- [x] t2038 research: pick path to bypass branch protection for github-actions[bot] — rulesets vs fine-grained PAT — research/decide task; deliverable is a documented decision + AGENTS.md update + child implementation task. Two viable paths for unblocking `github-actions[bot]` pushes to main: (1) migrate classic protection to GitHub Rulesets with `bypass_actors` containing `github-actions` (~2-3h one-time, no ongoing cost, future-proof since GitHub is sunsetting classic protection); (2) fine-grained PAT stored as a repo secret (~30m one-time, ongoing rotation cost, secret management surface). Picking the wrong one creates either ongoing rotation fatigue or a moderately risky migration. Belongs to maintainer judgment on threat model, not LLM guess. Task starts with a 30-second curl test to verify GitHub hasn't silently fixed `bypass_pull_request_allowances` on classic protection since 2026-04-13 — if it has, problem disappears. Reasoning tier because deliverable is a recommendation with rationale (Sonnet enumerates without committing). Implementation is a downstream child task filed by t2038 itself. Until both ship, every merged PR with a tNNN title hits the t2029 loud-failure path and requires manual `task-complete-helper.sh`. ~10-30 manual command-runs per day on this repo's merge volume. #research #ci #interactive ~2.5h tier:reasoning ref:GH#18522 logged:2026-04-13 -> [todo/tasks/t2038-brief.md] pr:#18647 completed:2026-04-13

- [x] t2048 implement: fine-grained PAT path for github-actions[bot] main push (from t2038 decision) — Path B chosen over Path C (rulesets + deploy key) in t2038 on setup-cost asymmetry (~20-30m vs ~2-3h) and rollback simplicity. Path A (rulesets + Integration bypass) disqualified: personal-account repos return `422 Validation Failed — Actor GitHub Actions integration must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization`. Two deliverables: (1) workflow edit — `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` `Checkout main` step and `Update TODO.md proof-log` step env both switch from `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` to `${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` fallback, plus a `::notice::Using SYNC_PAT for push` log line gated on a `SYNC_PAT_PRESENT` env flag so operators can one-grep-confirm the swap landed; (2) maintainer-only manual step documented in the brief — create a repo-scoped fine-grained PAT (`Contents: Read and write`, 366d expiry, NO `Workflows: Write`), store as Actions secret `SYNC_PAT`. - [x] t2035 fix(shared-constants): auto-assign interactive issues in `gh_create_issue` wrapper — root-cause complement to #18507. Current wrapper at `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh:823-829` forwards args to `gh issue create` and appends the origin label, but never sets an assignee. Result: every issue created via the wrapper from an interactive maintainer session lands unassigned, which trips the maintainer-gate "no assignee" check at `maintainer-gate.yml:275-289` and blocks the linked PR with `REVIEW_REQUIRED`. Currently affecting seven open `origin:interactive` PRs across this and prior sessions (#18460, #18495, #18497, #18500, #18502, #18505, #18506). Fix: add a new `_gh_auto_assign_from_url` helper in `shared-constants.sh` that parses the URL `gh issue create` echoes, extracts owner/repo/number, and runs `gh issue edit ... --add-assignee <current-user>`. Call it from `gh_create_issue` ONLY when origin is `interactive` (workers continue to skip self-assignment so the dispatcher's deferred assignment logic isn't disturbed). Non-blocking on assignment failure. Verbatim diff in brief, mirror of `claim-task-id.sh:_auto_assign_issue` pattern. #bug #shared-constants #auto-dispatch #interactive ~20m tier:simple ref:GH#19491 pr:#18518 logged:2026-04-13 -> [todo/tasks/t2035-brief.md] completed:2026-07-06

- [x] t2036 docs(build.txt): add deployed-vs-source diagnostic rule for runtime investigations — sibling to #18508 covering a different failure mode. When investigating runtime symptoms (pulse logs, agent timeouts, failed dispatches), the deployed copy at `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/<file>` may differ from the source at `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/<file>` — and it's the deployed copy the pulse executes. Reading source-as-truth led to the multi-hour mis-investigation of #18473 → #18498/t2025 cascade in this session: the bug was already fixed by t2019 / commit `a084f425f` and deployed at 02:09 (verified post-failure via `stat -f '%Sm'`), but the investigation began from log entries from 23:xx (pre-deploy) and never checked the deployed file mtime. Add a new numbered entry to the "Error Prevention" section of `.agents/prompts/build.txt` requiring a `stat -f '%Sm' ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/<file>` + `git -C ~/Git/aidevops log -1 --format='%ai' -- .agents/scripts/<file>` comparison BEFORE reading source for runtime debugging. ~14 lines added, fits the existing section voice. NEEDS-MAINTAINER-REVIEW (system-prompt edits affect every future session — not auto-dispatch, recursive footgun risk). Tier:standard, not simple — wording matters and needs editorial integration with the existing entries. #enhancement #docs #build.txt #interactive ~15m tier:standard ref:GH#19492 logged:2026-04-13 -> [todo/tasks/t2036-brief.md] pr:#19518 completed:2026-04-17

- [x] t2564 docs(opencode): document project_id drift and /sessions session visibility recovery — Opencode 1.14.19 identifies git-tracked projects by a git commit SHA stored in `session.project_id`; when opencode regenerates this SHA (binary update, rebase, certain reference events) prior sessions orphan off the TUI `/sessions` picker. Live diagnosis 2026-04-21 on aidevops repo: 696 sessions orphaned on old project_id after opencode-ai binary update on 2026-04-20; one-line SQL `UPDATE session SET project_id='NEW' WHERE project_id='OLD'` restored full visibility. Archive DB needs no action — TUI doesn't read it. Add `## Project ID drift — /sessions loses history` section to `.agents/reference/opencode-maintenance.md` with Symptom/Cause/Diagnose/Fix/Archive-DB subsections so the next hit is a 2-minute recovery instead of a multi-hour diagnosis. - [x] t2187 investigate(otel): opencode v1.4.11 `run` mode does not emit per-tool-call `Tool.execute`/`Bash` spans — empirical finding from t2186 verification session (2026-04-18). Headless-spawned worker produced 471 spans / 108 unique ops (Config, FileSystem, Agent, Auth, Session, ToolRegistry, SessionPrompt, Git, Npm, Bus) — but zero `Tool.execute.*`/`Bash.*`/`Read.*`/`Edit.*`/`Write.*`/`Grep.*` spans. Strings exist in the darwin-arm64 binary, so the gap is code-path specific (run vs TUI vs server), not missing instrumentation. Consequence: the plugin's `enrichActiveSpan` finds no active span on every tool call in headless run mode and silently no-ops — `aidevops.task_id` join key from OTEL to TODO.md is invisible. Plugin-side SQLite (`tool_calls` table) unaffected. Research plan: (1) survey opencode v1.4.11 source to locate Tool.execute instrumentation; determine whether gap is (a) deliberate / (b) bug / (c) config-gated; (2) decide plugin-owned span fallback vs accept gap; (3) contingency — check server mode. - [x] t2576 ## Task Update stale patterns in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-parent-nudge.sh` tests 3 & 4 so they pass against current source. ## Why Discovered during t2572 (PR #20249) implementation. Two tests in `test-pulse-parent-nudge.sh` fail on baseline (both before and after t2572), because their expected-pattern assertions have not been updated to match the current call signatures used in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`: - **Test 3** expects `gh api "repos/${REPO}/..."` (non-paginated) but the code has migrated to `gh api --paginate "repos/${REPO}/..."` as part of the dedup-count streaming fix. - **Test 4** expects `gh issue comment` calls but the code now uses the `gh_issue_comment` wrapper (from `shared-constants.sh`) which adds origin labelling and safer comment handling. Both failures are pre-existing and unrelated to t2572's `--slurp --jq` fix. They were noted out-of-scope in PR #20249 and flagged here for follow-up. ## What Audit `test-pulse-parent-nudge.sh` against the current implementation of the four helpers it covers: - `_post_parent_decomposition_nudge` - `_compute_parent_nudge_age_hours` - `_post_parent_decomposition_escalation` - `_post_parent_task_no_markers_warning` (in `issue-sync-lib.sh`) Update the structural assertions so they match the current `--paginate` + `gh_issue_comment` + streaming-dedup shape. Keep the behavioural intent — the test's job is to guard against regression of the idempotency / dedup logic, not to pin a specific gh-api syntax. ## How - EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-parent-nudge.sh` — fix tests 3 & 4 only (leave the others alone; 1, 2, and the test-parent-decomposition-nudge-dedup.sh from t2572 all pass). - Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-decomposition-nudge-dedup.sh` (landed in #20249) — uses current `--paginate` and streaming-pattern assertions; structure matches the intent of tests 3 & 4. - Verification: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-parent-nudge.sh` → all tests pass (was failing 3 & 4 on baseline). ## Acceptance - [ ] `test-pulse-parent-nudge.sh` runs cleanly with no failures on `main` - [ ] Tests 3 & 4 assertion text updated to match current `gh api --paginate` and `gh_issue_comment` call shapes - [ ] Test intent preserved — still guards the four helpers' idempotency/dedup behaviour - [ ] No regression: `test-parent-decomposition-nudge-dedup.sh` from t2572 still passes ## Files Scope - `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-parent-nudge.sh` ## Session Origin Interactive session, t2572 / PR #20249 implementation (2026-04-21). Pre-existing failure noted during rebase/test validation; filed as follow-up per finding-to-task completeness rule. ## Context Tier: `tier:simple` — small, mechanical test-expectation update with reference pattern already landed (`test-parent-decomposition-nudge-dedup.sh`). Single file, <100 line change expected. #auto-dispatch #framework ref:GH#20250 pr:#20282 completed:2026-04-21

- [x] t2724 ## What Render the session-start framework status as an OpenCode TUI toast via `client.tui.showToast()` instead of (or in addition to) injecting it as the first message in context. Phase 1 is additive — the toast appears alongside the existing message-context greeting so we can A/B the visual result. Phase 2 trims the human-only parts from the context version. ## Why The current session greeting — version string, security advisories, pulse status, contribution count — is rendered by the model as the first message in every interactive session. This consumes 100-200 tokens of context per session (more when advisories are active), even though most of the content is status information the human needs but the model rarely acts on. OpenCode 1.14 exposes `client.tui.showToast()` (SDK method `TuiShowToastData`, URL `/tui/show-toast`) with `variant: info|success|warning|error` and optional `duration`. Routing the banner through toasts frees that context entirely while keeping the human-visible information at session start. ## How Phase 1 — additive plugin hook: - NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs` — module exporting `createGreetingHook({ scriptsDir, client })`. Handler fires on `event.type === "session.created"`, guarded by a `fired` flag so it runs once per plugin init. Runs `${scriptsDir}/aidevops-update-check.sh --interactive`, parses the output into up to 3 toasts (info for version/env, warning for pulse/contribution, error for security advisories), emits via `await client.tui.showToast({ body: { title, message, variant, duration } })`. - EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` — import `createGreetingHook`, compose the greeting handler into the existing `event:` hook alongside the observability handler so both run on every event. - Model pattern to follow: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs` (same event-subscription style; see `handleEvent` signature). - Defaults: 3 toasts max, 10s duration (30s for errors), fire-once per plugin init. Phase 2 — trim redundant human-only lines from model-rendered greeting (separate commit in same PR once Phase 1 is visually confirmed): - EDIT: `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh:47-…` — the "On interactive conversation start" instruction block. Reduce to: "If the user asks about version/advisories/status, Read `~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting.txt`." Remove the "greet with: Hi!..." scripted response entirely (toast handles it). ### Files Scope - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs` - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` - `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh` - `todo/tasks/*-brief.md` - `TODO.md` ## Acceptance - Launching a fresh OpenCode session displays an info toast within 2s of first prompt render showing the aidevops version and runtime. - When security advisories are present, a separate error-variant toast appears with the advisory summary. - When the pulse is stalled or contributions need reply, a warning-variant toast appears. - Message-context consumption from the greeting drops by ≥50 tokens (measured via `opencode stats` before/after a clean session start with no advisories). - No regression: the existing observability `event:` handler still receives all events (verified via `~/.aidevops/logs/observability.sqlite` new rows on tool calls). - Plugin init completes without errors in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` or OpenCode's own log. ## Session Origin Interactive session, OpenCode v1.14.20, aidevops v3.8.91. Request from maintainer — "shall we add to toast first, see how that looks, then remove bit by bit that's for humans only?" ref:GH#20412 pr:#20420 completed:2026-04-22

- [x] t2771 ## What Deterministic phase-extractor scanner: when a `parent-task` issue body follows the well-formed phase template (explicit `### Phase N:` headings with required sub-sections), automatically file each phase as a standalone `tier:standard` child via verbatim text extraction. Zero LLM, zero paraphrasing. Complements the existing auto-decomposer which handles the general case. The existing decomposer is an LLM pass; this scanner is a deterministic short-circuit for parent bodies that already contain a fully-written phase plan. ## Why Canonical case: #20622 (GraphQL→REST routing). Parent body already contains 4 well-formed phases with `EDIT:` file paths, reference patterns, verification commands, and acceptance criteria. The existing auto-decomposer filed #20633 to do the work an LLM would need to invent — but the content is already written in the parent. Running an LLM over it adds hallucination surface for zero value. This scanner detects the template, verifies completeness, and files each phase with verbatim content. If any required sub-section is missing for a phase, the scanner no-ops and falls back to the existing decomposer. ## How ### Files to modify - NEW: `.agents/scripts/parent-task-phase-extractor.sh` — detect + verify + file. Deterministic: no LLM call. - EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` — add a call to the new helper before the existing `auto-decomposer` dispatch. If the extractor fires (exit 0), skip the decomposer for this parent. - NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-extractor.sh` — unit tests covering detection, completeness check, and fail-safe fallback. ### Detection algorithm (deterministic, no LLM) Parent body is eligible when it contains 2+ blocks matching ALL of: - `^### Phase d+:` heading line - `^- EDIT:` or `^- NEW:` (≥1 line in the phase section) - `^**Reference pattern:**` sub-section - `^**Verification:**` sub-section - `^**Acceptance:**` sub-section (with ≥1 criterion bullet) If any phase is missing any of these, the scanner NO-OPs entirely — does not file partial children, does not fall halfway through. This is the fail-safe for reliability: either the template is complete and extraction is trivially safe, or we don't touch it. ### Action (pure text extraction) For each qualifying phase: 1. Claim task ID: `claim-task-id.sh --repo-path <path> --title "<parent-title-prefix>: Phase <N> — <phase-heading>" --no-issue` 2. Compose body: verbatim copy of the phase section from parent + auto-generated `## Context` block linking parent via `For #<parent-num>` (NOT `Closes` / `Resolves` — parent-task keyword rule, see `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Parent-task PR keyword rule"). 3. Call `gh_create_issue` (via `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`) with labels `auto-dispatch,tier:standard` plus whatever tier label the parent carries (if tier:thinking parent, phases inherit). 4. Append `## Children` section to parent body if not present, or append new child line if section exists. ### Reference pattern Existing auto-decomposer pattern: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` `reconcile_parent_tasks` path. Mirror its dispatch shape but with the deterministic check first. ### Files Scope - .agents/scripts/parent-task-phase-extractor.sh - .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh - .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-extractor.sh ## Verification ``` shellcheck .agents/scripts/parent-task-phase-extractor.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh # Test: synthetic parent body with each required sub-section missing individually # assert scanner no-ops for each bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-extractor.sh # Test: canonical #20622 body (snapshot as fixture) # assert scanner files exactly 4 children with verbatim phase content ``` ## Acceptance Criteria 1. Scanner detects all 4 phases in a #20622-shaped parent body 2. Scanner no-ops when any required sub-section is missing from ANY phase (all-or-nothing) 3. Child issues contain verbatim phase text, no paraphrasing 4. Parent body gets `## Children` section added with cross-links to all filed children 5. Unit tests cover each missing-sub-section case plus the happy-path canonical case ### Non-scope - Do not modify the existing auto-decomposer. This is a short-circuit path, not a replacement. - Do not attempt to LLM-guess missing sub-sections. Missing → no-op. - Do not file children for parents carrying `no-auto-dispatch` — that's a user opt-out. ## Session Origin Filed from interactive review of pulse concurrency blockers. User asked for a scanner that was reliable with no hallucination risk; this design is pure regex + verbatim copy. #auto-dispatch #framework #pulse ref:GH#20641 pr:#20668 completed:2026-04-24

Re-dispatch will rewrite the same code from scratch. ## How EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` (or `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` if hooks exist there) - Add EXIT trap: before exit, if `git -C $WORKER_WORKTREE_PATH log main..HEAD` has commits, run: - `git push -u origin $branch_name 2>/dev/null || true` (best-effort, fail-open) - Log `[lifecycle] worker_exit_pushed_wip branch=$branch ahead=N` to stderr - Skip if `WORKER_NO_EXIT_PUSH=1` (escape hatch) - The 300s activity-watchdog kill path (`worker-activity-watchdog.sh`) should also push before SIGKILL Reference pattern: similar EXIT-trap pattern in `pulse-cleanup.sh::_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` (audit trail on early exit). ## Verification ```bash shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh # Manual: kill a running worker via SIGTERM, verify branch has remote gh api "repos/$slug/branches/$branch" --jq '.name' ``` ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] EXIT trap pushes any local-only commits to origin before worker exits - [ ] Watchdog kill path also pushes WIP before SIGKILL - [ ] `WORKER_NO_EXIT_PUSH=1` escape hatch documented - [ ] No regression on workers that complete normally (push happens once, not twice) - [ ] Test: kill worker mid-implementation, verify branch on remote with WIP commit #auto-dispatch #feat #framework ref:GH#21098 pr:#21121 completed:2026-04-26

- [x] t2966 ## Task t2874 Phase 1: define the Markdoc-compatible tag namespace and JSON schemas that all subsequent phases (validator, extractor, migration, consumers) depend on. ## Why Schema-first: a canonical schema set is the single source of truth that prevents each phase from inventing its own tag shapes. The validator (Phase 2) and extractor (Phase 3) both parse against these schemas; the migration (Phase 4) knows exactly which tag attributes to emit; the PageIndex consumer (Phase 5) knows which attributes to promote to node metadata. ## How 1. Create directory `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/` (NEW directory). 2. For each of the 7 initial tags, create a JSON schema file: - `sensitivity.json` — attrs: `tier` (required, enum: public/internal/confidential/privileged/redacted), `scope` (optional, file/section/inline). Scope rule: file or section or inline. - `provenance.json` — attrs: `source-id` (required, string), `extracted-at` (required, ISO date), `confidence` (optional, float 0–1). Scope rule: file or section. - `case-attach.json` — attrs: `case-id` (required, string), `relation` (optional, enum: evidence/timeline/exhibit/correspondence). Scope rule: section or inline. - `citation.json` — attrs: `source-id` (required), `page` (optional, string), `confidence` (optional, float). Scope rule: inline. - `redaction.json` — attrs: `reason` (required, string), `redacted-by` (optional, string). Scope rule: section or inline. - `draft-status.json` — attrs: `status` (required, enum: draft/review/approved/archived), `assignee` (optional, string). Scope rule: file or section. - `link.json` — attrs: `target` (required, string), `kind` (optional, enum: brand-asset/reference/source/exhibit). Scope rule: inline. 3. Each JSON schema file must include: `name`, `description`, `attributes` (with `type`, `required`, `enum` where applicable), `scope_rules` (allowed: file/section/inline), and an `example` showing valid Markdoc syntax. 4. Add a `schemas/README.md` that documents the namespace convention (`{% tag attr="value" %} ... {% /tag %}` for block, `{% tag attr="value" /%}` for self-closing) and lists the 7 tags with one-line descriptions. **Reference pattern:** model schema structure on existing JSON configs in `.agents/configs/`. Follow the Markdoc tag grammar from <https://markdoc.dev/docs/tags> (syntax reference only — no JS runtime needed). ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/` directory exists with 7 JSON schema files and a README.md. - [ ] Each schema has: `name`, `description`, `attributes` (with types + required flags), `scope_rules`, and `example`. - [ ] Schema file lints cleanly (`jq . <file>` exits 0 for each). - [ ] README.md documents the namespace convention and lists all 7 tags. ## Session Origin Decomposition child of t2874 (parent: #20966). Filed when t2840 MVP prerequisites landed (t2843 + t2849 + t2850 all CLOSED). ## Files to Modify - NEW: `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/sensitivity.json` - NEW: `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/provenance.json` - NEW: `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/case-attach.json` - NEW: `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/citation.json` - NEW: `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/redaction.json` - NEW: `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/draft-status.json` - NEW: `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/link.json` - NEW: `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/README.md` For #20966 #auto-dispatch #feat #framework ref:GH#21254 pr:#21350 completed:2026-04-27

- [x] t2968 ## Task t2874 Phase 2: implement `markdoc-validate.sh` — schema conformance checker for Markdoc-tagged knowledge plane files, with pre-commit hook and CI gate integration. ## Why A validator that runs at write time prevents malformed tags from entering the corpus. An extractor (Phase 3) that runs without a validator will silently produce empty extractions when tags are malformed — RAG looks like it works but has missing data. Validator-first means malformed tags fail loudly at commit time. ## How 1. Read the Phase 1 schemas at `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/` (all 7 JSON files). 2. Create `.agents/scripts/markdoc-validate.sh`: - **Usage:** `markdoc-validate.sh validate <file>` - **Parser:** regex-based Markdoc tag parser (no JS runtime). Extract all `{% tag_name ... %}`, `{% /tag_name %}`, and self-closing `{% tag_name ... /%}` patterns. - **Checks per tag:** - Unknown tag name (not in schema set) → error with file:line:column - Missing required attribute → error with file:line:column - Attribute value not in enum → error with file:line:column - Unclosed block tag (opened but no matching close) → error - Wrong scope (file-level tag inside a section that doesn't allow file scope) → warning - **Exit codes:** 0 = valid, 1 = schema errors, 2 = parse errors - **Output format:** `<file>:<line>:<col>: [error|warning] <message>` (one per line, grep-friendly) 3. Pre-commit hook: add `markdoc-validate.sh validate` call to `install-hooks-helper.sh` for repos that opt in. Hook runs on staged `*.md` files in `_knowledge/`, `_cases/`, `_projects/`, `_performance/`, `_feedback/`, `_campaigns/`, `_inbox/`. 4. CI gate: `.github/workflows/markdoc-validate.yml` — runs on PRs touching knowledge plane paths. 5. ShellCheck zero violations. Local var pattern. Explicit returns. **Reference pattern:** model script structure on `.agents/scripts/qlty-regression-helper.sh` (ratchet gate pattern). Model hook integration on `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh`. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `.agents/scripts/markdoc-validate.sh validate <file>` exits 0 on a well-formed tagged file. - [ ] Exits 1 with `file:line:col: error:` output on missing required attribute. - [ ] Exits 1 with error on unknown tag name. - [ ] Exits 1 on unclosed block tag. - [ ] ShellCheck zero violations (`shellcheck .agents/scripts/markdoc-validate.sh`). - [ ] Pre-commit hook wired in `install-hooks-helper.sh` (opt-in). - [ ] CI workflow at `.github/workflows/markdoc-validate.yml`. ## Session Origin Decomposition child of t2874 (parent: #20966). Depends on Phase 1 (t2966/#21254 — schemas must exist). ## Files to Modify - NEW: `.agents/scripts/markdoc-validate.sh` - EDIT: `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh` — add markdoc-validate hook registration - NEW: `.github/workflows/markdoc-validate.yml` **Blocked by:** Phase 1 t2966/#21254 (schemas must be defined first). - [x] t2970 ## Task t2874 Phase 3: implement `markdoc-extract.sh` — produces tag-stripped plain text and a JSON sidecar listing all tag positions, attributes, and scope hierarchy from a Markdoc-tagged file. ## Why The extractor is the agent-stable query surface for tagged content. RAG consumers (PageIndex in Phase 5, retrieval in Phase 6) cannot reliably scan raw tag syntax on every lookup. The extractor produces two stable artefacts: (1) tag-stripped body text for embedding/search, (2) a `tags.json` sidecar with structured tag data for filter queries. ## How 1. Read the Phase 1 schemas at `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/` and Phase 2 validator at `.agents/scripts/markdoc-validate.sh`. 2. Create `.agents/scripts/markdoc-extract.sh`: - **Usage:** `markdoc-extract.sh extract <file> [--output-dir DIR] [--tree]` - **Outputs (written to same directory as `<file>` unless `--output-dir` is set):** - `<basename>.txt` — tag-stripped plain text (all `{% ... %}` removed, content inside block tags preserved) - `<basename>-tags.json` — array of `{tag, attrs, scope, char_start, char_end, line_start, line_end}` objects. Self-closing = `char_start === char_end`. - **`--tree` flag:** additionally writes `<basename>-tree.json` — hierarchical nesting: file-scope tags at root, section-scope tags as children of the enclosing heading, inline-scope tags as children of the enclosing section. - **Behaviour:** runs `markdoc-validate.sh validate <file>` first; exits non-zero if validation fails (never extract malformed input). - **Exit codes:** 0 = success, 1 = validation failed (see validator output), 2 = parse error 3. ShellCheck zero violations. Local var pattern. Explicit returns. 4. Add brief unit tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-markdoc-extract.sh`: - Well-formed file → txt + tags.json both written, exit 0. - File with unknown tag → exits 1 (validator stops it). - `--tree` flag → tree.json written. **Reference pattern:** model output pattern on `.agents/scripts/knowledge-pageindex-helper.sh` (JSON sidecar writing). Model test structure on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-parent-task.sh`. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `markdoc-extract.sh extract <well-formed-file>` exits 0, writes `<basename>.txt` and `<basename>-tags.json`. - [ ] tags.json is valid JSON (`jq . <file>` exits 0). - [ ] `--tree` flag writes `<basename>-tree.json` (valid JSON). - [ ] Malformed input (validation fail) exits 1, no output files written. - [ ] ShellCheck zero violations. - [ ] Tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-markdoc-extract.sh` pass. ## Session Origin Decomposition child of t2874 (parent: #20966). Depends on Phase 2 (t2968/#21256 — validator must exist). ## Files to Modify - NEW: `.agents/scripts/markdoc-extract.sh` - NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-markdoc-extract.sh` **Blocked by:** Phase 2 t2968/#21256 (validator must exist — extractor calls it internally). For #20966 #auto-dispatch #feat #framework ref:GH#21258 pr:#21358 completed:2026-04-27

- [x] t2972 ## Task t2874 Phase 5: wire PageIndex tree generation (t2850/P1c) to lift Markdoc tag attributes from `source.md` into per-node metadata, so retrieval can filter and rank by tag attributes without re-reading file bodies. ## Why PageIndex (t2850) already builds a per-document tree with summaries. Without tag lifting, tag attributes are invisible to the index — retrieval must re-parse every source.md to apply tag filters, which is expensive and fragile. With tag lifting, tag attributes become first-class node metadata: `{sensitivity: 'privileged', case: 'acme-dispute'}` is readable from the index directly, enabling `knowledge search --sensitivity privileged` without full-corpus re-reads. ## How 1. Read the t2850 PageIndex implementation: find the main PageIndex helper script (likely `.agents/scripts/knowledge-pageindex-helper.sh` or similar — confirm with `git ls-files '*pageindex*'`). 2. Extend the PageIndex build step to: - Call `markdoc-extract.sh extract <source.md>` for each source (or read existing `-tags.json` sidecar if fresh). - For file-scope tags: inject `{tag, attrs}` into the root PageIndex node `metadata` field for that document. - For section-scope tags: inject into the subtree node whose heading range contains the tag. - For inline-scope tags: inject into the nearest leaf node. 4. Extend the PageIndex JSON schema (if one exists) to include `metadata` as an optional map field per node. 5. Citation tags: in the tree output, add a `cross_references` array at the document root listing all `{% citation source-id="..." %}` attrs (structured cross-reference index). 6. ShellCheck zero violations. Local var pattern. Explicit returns. **Reference pattern:** read the existing PageIndex builder (from t2850 output) to understand the node structure before extending it. Model metadata injection on how the existing `summary` field is set per node. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Running PageIndex build on a `source.md` with a file-scope `{% sensitivity tier="privileged" /%}` tag produces a root node with `metadata.sensitivity.tier == "privileged"`. - [ ] Section-scope tags appear on the subtree node, not the root. - [ ] Citation tags produce a `cross_references` array at document root. - [ ] ShellCheck zero violations on modified scripts. ## Session Origin Decomposition child of t2874 (parent: #20966). - [x] t2979 ## Task t2874 Phase 7: implement `markdoc-render-gh.sh` — a GitHub comment renderer that strips or pretty-prints Markdoc tags when reproducing source content in PR/issue threads, so tag syntax doesn't leak into human-readable output. ## Why When `aidevops case draft` or knowledge search reproduces source content in a GH comment, raw Markdoc tag syntax (`{% sensitivity tier="privileged" /%}`) is noisy and confusing to human reviewers. A renderer transforms tags into readable annotations (e.g., `[PRIVILEGED]` badge) or strips them entirely for clean reading, depending on the output context. ## How 1. Create `.agents/scripts/markdoc-render-gh.sh`: - **Usage:** `markdoc-render-gh.sh render <file> [--strip | --annotate]` - **`--strip` (default):** removes all Markdoc tags, outputs clean prose text suitable for embedding in GH comments. Preserves content inside block tags. - **`--annotate`:** replaces each tag with a compact GH-flavoured badge: - `{% sensitivity tier="privileged" /%}` → `**[PRIVILEGED]**` - `{% draft-status status="draft" /%}` → `*[DRAFT]*` - `{% case-attach case-id="acme" /%}` → `*[Case: acme]*` - Unknown tag → stripped (safe default) - **Input:** path to a `source.md` file or stdin (`-`) - **Output:** stdout (for pipe into `gh issue comment --body` or similar) 2. Wire into `aidevops case draft` comment output: before posting the draft body to a GH comment, pipe through `markdoc-render-gh.sh render --annotate`. 3. Wire into `aidevops knowledge search` snippet output: when printing a source excerpt, pipe through `markdoc-render-gh.sh render --strip`. 4. ShellCheck zero violations. **Note:** IDE LSP autocomplete (originally part of Phase 7 scope in the parent brief) is deferred — it requires a language server integration not in scope for shell-based tooling. Renderer is the actionable deliverable. **Reference pattern:** model tag pattern matching on the Phase 3 extractor (`markdoc-extract.sh`) tag regex. Model GH badge syntax on existing comment formatters in `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh`. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `markdoc-render-gh.sh render --strip <tagged-file>` outputs tag-free prose, exit 0. - [ ] `markdoc-render-gh.sh render --annotate <tagged-file>` outputs annotated prose with badge strings, exit 0. - [ ] Piping tagged content through renderer produces valid GH markdown (no raw `{% %}` syntax in output). - [ ] ShellCheck zero violations. - [ ] `aidevops case draft` uses `--annotate` mode for comment output. ## Session Origin Decomposition child of t2874 (parent: #20966). Can be implemented in parallel with Phases 4-6 (only depends on Phase 3 extractor). Listed last because it is lowest-priority tooling. ## Files to Modify - NEW: `.agents/scripts/markdoc-render-gh.sh` - EDIT: case draft agent script — pipe output through renderer before posting GH comment - EDIT: `.agents/scripts/knowledge-helper.sh` — pipe search snippet output through renderer **Blocked by:** Phase 3 t2970/#21258 (renderer uses same tag regex as extractor — implement after extractor is stable). Closes #20966 #auto-dispatch #feat #framework ref:GH#21269 pr:#21360 completed:2026-04-27

The `|| echo "0"` fallback then appended a SECOND "0", producing `"0\n0"`. Fix: replace both with `|| true` and default-if-empty (`"${var:-0}"`) — single-line grep output, no double-source of "0". - [x] t3005 ## Task The `_dispatch_fill_floor` loop in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` processes candidates **serially** — each `_dff_process_candidate` call blocks until completion before the next iteration starts. With ~100s per successful dispatch (most of it in `worktree-helper.sh add`), 24 worker slots take 40 minutes of wall-clock time to fill. With pulse cycle interval of ~7-15min, we never reach the concurrency ceiling. ## Why (incident evidence) Direct measurements 2026-04-28T01:21Z (after deploying t3003 adaptive timeout v3.13.5): - `Stage complete: fill_floor_candidate_21436 (0, 109s)` — single dispatch took 109 seconds - 24 worker slots available, only 2 workers running steady-state - 132 dispatchable issues across 2 repos, 80% of pulse cycles dispatch 0-1 workers - Root cause: serial loop at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:816` — `_dff_process_candidate` blocks the loop body The 109s dispatch breakdown: - `Stage start` → `Pre-created worktree`: ~100s (worktree-helper.sh add) - `Pre-created worktree` → `Stage complete`: ~5-9s (gh API ops + nohup spawn) With serial dispatch: - Best case: 1 successful dispatch per pulse cycle (~7min) = 8/hour - Required for 24 concurrency: 48/hour (assuming 30min worker duration) - **Throughput gap: 6x** ## How ### Files Scope - EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh::_dispatch_fill_floor` — parallelize the candidate loop with bounded concurrency (lines ~750-836) - EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh::_dff_process_candidate` — make safe for concurrent invocation (state mutations) - NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-fill-floor-parallel.sh` — regression test for parallel dispatch ### Approach **Bounded parallelism with shared state file:** ```bash local _dff_max_parallel=6 # tunable: 6 concurrent dispatches × ~100s each = 1 cycle of 24 local _pids=() while IFS= read -r candidate_json; do if [[ "${#_pids[@]}" -ge "$_dff_max_parallel" ]]; then wait -n # bash 4+: wait for any one to finish _pids=("${_pids[@]/$!}") # remove finished pid fi if [[ "$dispatched_count" -ge "$_effective_slots" ]]; then break; fi # Background dispatch + record outcome via shared state file ( _dff_proc_rc=0 _dff_process_candidate "$candidate_json" "$self_login" "$available_slots" || _dff_proc_rc=$? if [[ "$_dff_proc_rc" -eq 0 ]]; then echo "success" >> "$_dff_outcomes_file" fi ) & _pids+=($!) done <"$_dff_candidate_file" wait # for remaining dispatched_count=$(wc -l < "$_dff_outcomes_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ``` **State mutation safety:** `_dff_process_candidate` mutates module globals (`_DFF_ROUND_DISPATCHED`, `_DFF_THROTTLE_CLEARED`, `_DFF_CONSECUTIVE_NO_WORKER`, `_PULSE_LAST_LAUNCH_FAILURE`). In a backgrounded subshell, these mutations are isolated and lost. Solutions: 1. **Outcomes file** (preferred): aggregate state via shared file, post-loop reconciliation 2. **Drop throttle tracking**: if throttle is rare-path, simpler to remove 3. **flock-based mutex**: atomic increments via `flock` + arithmetic Outcomes file is simplest: each backgrounded dispatch appends one line indicating success/skip/timeout, post-loop sums. Loses real-time throttle decisions but throttle only matters for SUCCESSIVE-failure detection, which can run on completed batch. ### Reference patterns - `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh::_refresh_owner_*` — already uses backgrounded gh search calls with `wait` for parallel I/O - `.agents/scripts/dispatch-timing-helper.sh::_acquire_lock` — mkdir-lock pattern for concurrent state writes - `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` — fire-and-forget background pattern with PID tracking ### Configuration New env var: `DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL` (default 6). Override in plist via `EnvironmentVariables`. - Set to `1` to retain serial behavior (regression escape hatch). - Set to `12` for aggressive (~50% utilization while preserving slot accounting). - Cap at `_effective_slots` (don't dispatch more concurrent attempts than slots). ### Verification - `tests/test-fill-floor-parallel.sh` regression: launch N=6 mock candidates, all should complete via `wait`, dispatched_count should match success count - Live: after deploy, observe `pulse-stage-timings.log` — `_dispatch_fill_floor` total duration should drop from ~10min to ~2min when queue has dispatchable candidates - Live: workers should ramp from 2 to 24 within 1-2 pulse cycles (currently takes hours) ## Acceptance - [ ] Fill floor processes ≥ 6 candidates in parallel by default - [ ] State mutations (throttle, dispatched_count) preserved across parallel dispatch - [ ] No regression: serial mode (`DISPATCH_FILL_FLOOR_PARALLEL=1`) still works - [ ] Regression test added covering parallel dispatch + outcome aggregation - [ ] ShellCheck zero new violations - [ ] Function-complexity gate: `_dispatch_fill_floor` stays under 100 lines (or refactor to sub-function) - [ ] Live verification: workers reach 12+ concurrent within 2 pulse cycles after deployment ## Files Scope - .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh - .agents/scripts/tests/test-fill-floor-parallel.sh ## Complexity Impact - `_dispatch_fill_floor`: currently ~120 lines, projected ~140 lines after adding parallel loop. May need extraction to `_dff_dispatch_one_parallel` helper to stay under 100-line gate. Plan refactor pre-implementation. ## Session Origin Discovered during v3.13.5 verification (t3003 follow-up). Adaptive timeout (180s budget) successfully unblocked individual launches, but serial fill_floor caps total throughput at 8-15 workers/hour. With 24-slot pool and 132 dispatchable issues, the system is structurally incapable of reaching max concurrency. Demo tomorrow requires immediate fix. #auto-dispatch #bug #priority:critical #pulse #auto-dispatch #bug #priority:critical #pulse ref:GH#21438 pr:#21450 testing:runtime-verified completed:2026-04-28

Five contributing causes: (1) no batch auto-detection in `cmd_pulse()`, (2) auto-batch absorption has no affinity checks, (3) `cmd_next()` sibling limits ignore batch concurrency, (4) `blocked-by:` not enforced in dispatch path, (5) AI lifecycle auto-merge has no human review gate. When the supervisor calls `cmd_push` from the aidevops repo directory but TODO.md contains tasks belonging to other repos (via cross-repo DB), all issues get created in the wrong repo. Fix: for each task being pushed, check the supervisor DB for the task's actual repo. If the task's repo doesn't match the current `repo_slug`, skip it (or push to the correct repo). - [x] t1200 IP reputation check agent — vet VPS/server/proxy IPs before purchase/deployment. Create `tools/security/ip-reputation.md` agent and `ip-reputation-helper.sh` CLI that queries multiple IP reputation providers in parallel, merges results into a unified risk report, and caches in SQLite. Use case: before buying a VPS, dedicated server, or proxy pool, check if the IPs are already burned (blacklisted, flagged as spam/abuse/proxy/VPN, listed on DNSBLs). Follows the same orchestrator+provider pattern as tech-stack-helper.sh (t1063). Providers (all curl/DNS-queryable, no browser automation needed): (1) **IPQualityScore** (ipqualityscore.com) — fraud score, proxy/VPN/Tor detection, abuse velocity, bot detection. Free tier: 5000 lookups/month. REST API. (2) **Scamalytics** (scamalytics.com) — fraud score 0-100, proxy/VPN detection, ISP risk. Free tier available. Investigate API endpoints via network analysis of their web lookup tool to avoid browser automation. (3) **AbuseIPDB** (abuseipdb.com) — community-reported abuse, confidence score 0-100. Free: 1000 checks/day. REST API. (4) **ProxyCheck.io** (proxycheck.io) — proxy/VPN/Tor detection, risk score 0-100. Free: 1000 req/day, no key required. REST API. (5) **GreyNoise** (greynoise.io) — mass scanner/bot detection, malicious classification. Free: 10000 req/month. REST API. (6) **Spamhaus/DNSBL** — PBL/SBL/CBL/XBL via DNS lookup (dig reversed-ip.zen.spamhaus.org). Free for non-commercial. (7) **Shodan** (shodan.io) — open ports, hosting infra, known malicious services. Free tier. REST API. (8) **IP Hub** (iphub.info) — residential vs proxy/VPN classification. Free: 1000 req/day. (9) **StopForumSpam** (stopforumspam.com) — spammer IP database. Free API, no key. (10) **Blocklist.de** (blocklist.de) — attack/botnet IP feeds. Free API. Also integrate with existing `email-health-check-helper.sh blacklist` command for DNSBL overlap. Output: unified risk report with per-provider scores, overall risk rating (clean/low/medium/high/critical), VPN/proxy/Tor flags, blacklist hits, abuse reports, and recommendation (safe to use / proceed with caution / avoid). Commands: `ip-reputation-helper.sh check <ip>` (single IP), `ip-reputation-helper.sh batch <file>` (bulk from file, one IP per line), `ip-reputation-helper.sh report <ip>` (detailed markdown report), `ip-reputation-helper.sh providers` (list configured providers and API key status). - [x] t167 Investigate Gemini Code Assist for full codebase review in daily pulse #quality #automation #research ~30m (ai:20m read:10m) ref:GH#625 assignee:marcusquinn logged:2026-02-08 started:2026-02-08 completed:2026-02-08 verified:2026-02-08 PR #650 merged
  - Notes: **Research complete (2026-02-08).** Gemini Code Assist GitHub bot (`gemini-code-assist[bot]`) only reviews PR diffs -- confirmed via official docs (developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-github-code, updated 2026-02-02). No full codebase review API or trigger exists. Commands limited to `/gemini review`, `/gemini summary`, `@gemini-code-assist` -- all PR-scoped. Consumer quota: 33 PR reviews/day; Enterprise: 100+/day. **Three approaches evaluated:**
  - **Option 1: Synthetic full-diff PR** -- Create branch from empty tree (`git commit-tree $(git hash-object -t tree /dev/null)`), PR against main. Forces Gemini to review entire codebase as a "diff". VIABLE but hacky: creates noise in PR history, may hit review size limits, 33/day consumer quota means 1 daily review is feasible. Recommended as interim approach for t166 integration.
  - **Option 2: Gemini CLI (gemini-cli)** -- Open-source CLI agent with ReAct loop, file read/write, MCP support. Free tier: 1000 requests/day, 60/min. Can be prompted to review codebase locally without GitHub bot. MOST VIABLE for daily pulse: run `gemini review the codebase for quality issues` in repo dir, parse structured output. No PR needed. Integrates via supervisor dispatch like any other CLI tool.
  - **Option 3: Gemini API directly** -- Use Gemini 3 Pro/Flash via API with 1M token context window. Feed repo contents, get structured review. VIABLE but requires API key management and custom integration code. Higher cost than CLI approach.
  - **Recommendation:** Option 2 (Gemini CLI) is the best path for t166 integration. It's free, local, scriptable, and avoids the PR-only limitation of the GitHub bot. Add as t166 subtask: `gemini-cli-helper.sh review` command that runs Gemini CLI codebase review, parses output into same structured format as CodeRabbit findings. Option 1 (synthetic PR) is a viable fallback if CLI output quality is insufficient. Option 3 is overkill for this use case.
  - **Quality assessment:** Gemini's review on PR #622 caught a real regex issue (high severity) but also produced false positives. Same bot-review verification rules from t166.2 apply. Gemini focuses on: correctness, efficiency, maintainability, security. Customizable via `.gemini/styleguide.md` (already have `.gemini/settings.json` in repo). Enterprise version supports cross-repo style guides via Google Cloud console.

- [x] t060 Research jj (Jujutsu) VCS for aidevops advantages #research #git #tools ~15m (ai:10m read:5m) ref:GH#514 logged:2026-01-13 ref:https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj verified:2026-02-08
  - Notes: Git-compatible VCS (25.6k stars, v0.38.0, Apache-2.0, 300+ contributors, backed by Google). Written in Rust, uses gitoxide for Git backend. Key features: working-copy-as-commit (no staging area), operation log with full undo, conflicts as first-class objects, automatic rebase of descendants, anonymous branches (bookmarks), revset query language, safe concurrent replication.
  - Evaluation for aidevops:
    - RECOMMENDED: Colocated mode (`jj git init --colocate`) as bridge strategy. Maintains full git compatibility (all 39 scripts + 67 docs still work), allows gradual adoption, preserves GitHub/CI integration. jj and git commands work interchangeably in same repo.
    - HIGH VALUE: Operation log + undo eliminates the destructive command risk that spawned t009 (PreToolUse hooks). `jj undo` reverses any operation including the equivalent of `git reset --hard`. Would reduce need for pre-edit-check.sh defensive machinery (206 lines).
    - HIGH VALUE: jj workspaces (`jj workspace add`) are lighter than git worktrees. Could simplify the 3-tier fallback chain (wt -> worktree-helper.sh -> raw git worktree) in supervisor-helper.sh parallel dispatch.
    - MEDIUM VALUE: No staging area simplifies commit workflow. Working copy is always a commit, eliminating "dirty working copy" errors and `git stash` usage (7 files). Automatic rebase of descendants eliminates manual `git rebase main` after fetching (9 files).
    - MEDIUM VALUE: First-class conflicts enable committing conflicted state, resolving later. Valuable for supervisor parallel task dispatch where agents touch overlapping files. Conflict resolution propagates through descendants automatically.
    - MEDIUM VALUE: Change IDs persist through squash-merge/rebase/amend, solving the squash-merge detection problem in worktree-helper.sh `cmd_clean()` (currently uses fragile heuristics).
    - CONCERN: No git hooks support yet (issue #405). Pre-commit hooks are used by aidevops for quality gates. Workaround: run linters via jj's `run` command (design doc exists) or keep colocated mode where git hooks still fire.
    - CONCERN: No git submodules support yet. Not a blocker for aidevops (no submodules used).
    - CONCERN: No .gitattributes support (issue #53). Minor impact.
    - CONCERN: Still experimental (pre-1.0). Core devs use it daily, but storage format may change before 1.0. Colocated mode mitigates this -- can always fall back to pure git.
    - CONCERN: Learning curve for team. jj concepts (changes vs commits, bookmarks vs branches, revsets) differ from git mental model. Mitigated by colocated mode allowing gradual adoption.
  - Recommendation: Add jj as OPTIONAL tool in setup.sh alongside Worktrunk. Create a `tools/git/jj.md` subagent documenting jj equivalents for common aidevops git operations. Do NOT replace git -- use colocated mode as an enhancement layer. Revisit after jj 1.0 for deeper integration.
  - Follow-up tasks: t060.1 Add jj installation to setup.sh (optional), t060.2 Create tools/git/jj.md subagent, t060.3 Test jj colocated mode with supervisor parallel dispatch.

- [x] t124 Add Tirith terminal security guard for homograph/injection attacks #security #tools #terminal ~20m (ai:15m test:3m read:2m) ref:GH#522 logged:2026-02-03 ref:https://github.com/sheeki03/tirith completed:2026-02-08 verified:2026-02-08 PR #605 merged
  - Notes: Tirith (1,300 stars, Rust, AGPL-3.0) - also see t104 plan: Tirith's `tirith run` command provides verified download-then-execute as the implementation vehicle for curl|sh hardening. - terminal security tool that catches attacks browsers block but terminals don't. **30 rules across 7 categories:** 1) Homograph attacks (Cyrillic/Greek lookalikes, punycode, mixed-script). 2) Terminal injection (ANSI escapes, bidi overrides, zero-width chars). 3) Pipe-to-shell (`curl|bash`, `wget|sh`, `eval $(wget ...)`). 4) Dotfile attacks (downloads targeting ~/.bashrc, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys). 5) Insecure transport (HTTP piped to shell, `curl -k`). 6) Ecosystem threats (git clone typosquats, untrusted Docker registries, pip/npm URL installs). 7) Credential exposure (userinfo tricks, shortened URLs). **Integration options:** 1) Add to aidevops setup/onboarding as recommended install. 2) Create tirith.md subagent at tools/security/. 3) Document shell hook setup (`eval "$(tirith init)"`). 4) Consider MCP wrapper for `tirith check` command validation. **Key features:** Sub-millisecond overhead, local-only (no network calls), YAML policy config, bypass with `TIRITH=0` prefix. Install: `brew install sheeki03/tap/tirith` or `npm install -g tirith` or `cargo install tirith`.

Covers: color contrast (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 AA 4.5:1 normal/3:1 large, SC 1.4.6 AAA 7:1/4.5:1, SC 1.4.11 non-text contrast 3:1), keyboard navigation, ARIA roles/labels, heading hierarchy, alt text, form labels, focus indicators, link purpose, language attributes, reading order, motion/animation preferences.   - [x] t215.3 Playwright contrast extraction — computed style analysis for all visible elements ~20m ref:GH#906 assignee:marcusquinn started:2026-02-10T14:58:48Z completed:2026-02-10 pr:#937
    - Notes: Use Playwright page.evaluate() to traverse all visible DOM elements, extract computed foreground color (color) and background color (backgroundColor, walking up ancestors for transparent backgrounds), font size and weight (to determine "large text" threshold: >=18pt or >=14pt bold). Calculate contrast ratio per WCAG formula: (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) where L = relative luminance. Flag failures at AA (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large) and AAA (7:1 normal, 4.5:1 large). Also check non-text contrast (SC 1.4.11) for UI components and graphical objects at 3:1. Handle edge cases: gradients (sample multiple points), background images (flag as manual review), opacity, CSS filters. Output: element selector, actual colors, computed ratio, threshold, pass/fail, WCAG criterion. Cross-validate individual pairs against WebAIM Contrast Checker API for accuracy.

Items include id (rule code), description, count, selectors (XPath + CSS). Map WAVE rule IDs to WCAG success criteria for compliance reporting. Cache results to avoid burning credits on repeated scans. Rate limit: respect API limits.

- [x] t219 PR lifecycle — faster merge pipeline with parallel CI + review triage #enhancement #supervisor #throughput ~1.5h (ai:1h test:30m) ref:GH#914 assignee:marcusquinn started:2026-02-10T04:39:17Z logged:2026-02-10 completed:2026-02-10 pr:#922
  - Notes: The PR lifecycle (pr_review → review_triage → merging → merged → deploying → deployed) processes one stage per pulse (every 5 min). A PR with passing CI and no review threads takes 3+ pulses (15+ min) to go from complete to deployed. Improve: (1) Allow multi-stage transitions within a single pulse — if CI passes and no review threads, go straight from pr_review to merging in one pulse. (2) After merge, immediately run deploy + verify in the same pulse instead of waiting for the next one. - [x] t1741 feat: autoresearch — autonomous experiment loop for code, agent, and standalone research — `/autoresearch` command and subagent inspired by karpathy/autoresearch and hyperspaceai/agi. Three modes: in-repo (worktree optimization), cross-repo (target another managed repo), standalone (scaffold new `autoresearch-{name}` repo with `aidevops init`). - [x] t1178 Add completed-task filter to supervisor AI context builder to stop acting on verified tasks #enhancement #auto-dispatch #self-improvement ~1h model:sonnet category:automation — The supervisor AI context snapshot includes no exclusion of recently completed tasks. The context builder should cross-reference the supervisor DB verified/cancelled states and exclude those task IDs from the open tasks and dispatchable lists. This is complementary to t1148 (exclusion list in reasoning) and t1138 (cycle-level dedup) but operates at the context generation layer, preventing the AI from even seeing stale targets. Expected savings: eliminates ~40% of repeated actions visible in self-reflection data. ref:GH#1767 pr:#1779 completed:2026-02-19

- [x] t1179 Add cycle-aware dedup to supervisor — skip targets acted on in previous cycle unless state changed #enhancement #auto-dispatch #self-improvement ~2h model:sonnet category:automation — Self-reflection shows 13 targets receiving repeated actions across 5 cycles. Several are already-completed tasks (t1143, t1142, t1125) or issues already addressed by merged PRs (t1144 resolved the audit findings for #1695, #1572). The supervisor should maintain a last-action-per-target cache and skip targets where: (1) the same action type was proposed in the prior cycle, AND (2) the target's state hasn't changed since. This is distinct from t1138 (which adds general dedup) — this specifically addresses the cycle-over-cycle repetition pattern visible in self-reflection data. Expected benefit: eliminates ~60% of redundant actions per cycle, saving ~2000 tokens/cycle in context and execution. ref:GH#1772 assignee:marcusquinn started:2026-02-18T19:19:10Z pr:#1780 completed:2026-02-18

Add a reconciliation step to the supervisor pulse that syncs DB queue state with TODO.md reality — cancel DB entries for completed/cancelled TODO tasks, and flag tasks that are queued in DB but not dispatchable in TODO.md. - [x] t1181 Add action-target cooldown to supervisor reasoning to prevent acting on same target within N cycles #enhancement #auto-dispatch #self-improvement ~1h model:sonnet category:automation — The self-reflection shows 14 targets receiving repeated actions across 5 cycles. While t1178 and t1179 address this at the context-building and dedup layers, a simple cooldown mechanism provides a third safety net: if a target was acted on in the previous cycle and its state hasn't changed, skip it. Implementation: maintain a last_acted map in the supervisor DB with (target, cycle_number, action_type). Before proposing an action, check if the same (target, action_type) was executed in the last N cycles (default N=2) with no state change. If so, suppress the action. - [x] t2897 pulse: per-runner zero-attempt failure circuit breaker triggers update check — adds a new `pulse-runner-health-helper.sh` and three `pulse-wrapper.sh` integration points that track consecutive zero-attempt worker dispatches (`launch_recovery:no_worker_process`, no branch created, near-zero token usage, watchdog-killed before first commit). After 10 consecutive zero-attempts in a 6h window the runner pauses dispatch, runs `aidevops update` synchronously, auto-resumes if the update changed VERSION (t2579 hook handles restart), or stays paused with an advisory if the runner is on latest (real local problem). Closes the §4.4 cross-runner-coordination gap where a stale/broken runner keeps burning workers without anyone noticing. Brief: `todo/tasks/t2897-brief.md`. #bug #pulse #framework #multi-runner #interactive ~5h tier:thinking no-auto-dispatch logged:2026-04-26 pr:#21039 completed:2026-04-26 ref:GH#21047 -> [todo/tasks/t2897-brief.md]

- [x] t2898 aidevops update + setup.sh: verify auto-update daemon is enabled and warn if not — adds `auto-update-helper.sh health-check` (returns 0/1/2 per platform-specific launchd / systemd / cron detection plus state-file freshness), `--idempotent` flag on the existing `enable` subcommand, and two integration points: `setup.sh` end-of-run idempotently re-installs the daemon so every release self-heals broken installs, and `aidevops update` (when interactive) prints a yellow warning + writes a session-greeting advisory if the daemon is unhealthy. Closes the asymmetry where the user with the broken daemon is the user not seeing greetings. Brief: `todo/tasks/t2898-brief.md`. #enhancement #framework #reliability #auto-dispatch ~2h tier:standard logged:2026-04-26 pr:#21039 completed:2026-04-26 ref:GH#21048 -> [todo/tasks/t2898-brief.md]
